Exposure: Remind mother and Stephanie it is not a good idea to avoid the things Stephanie feels anxious about, as this will only make her anxiety stronger.
Mention relaxation apps available on mobile phones (Mindfulness for Children; Thrive Global); Encourage parent to practice these with their child.

Worry Box: Suggest the child and parent choose a specific time each day for the child to talk to her parent about her worries. Any other time when a worry pops into her mind, the child is supposed to imagine a box with a large lock on it. She is to put the worry into the box and leave it there until it is time to talk to her parent about it. Parents are to listen to and acknowledge their child’s worries and provide reassurance, comfort, and even problem-solving strategies if appropriate.

Continue long-acting methylphenidate (Concerta) 36 mg daily
Begin at starting dose, then increase to minimum effective dose if tolerated within 1-2 weeks

ICS: Educate the patient and family about anxiety – this includes normalizing anxiety and reassuring the patient that some anxiety is a good thing. We can talk about how small amounts of anxiety stop us from doing dangerous things or from getting in trouble at school. It can help motivate us to study so we do better in school. However, anxiety is not a good thing when it makes our bodies feel badly and when it stops us from doing things we want to do or need to do.
